key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can directly predict full-field dynamic response of polycrystalline microstructures, enabling fast optimization under competing strength targets.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to design stronger microstructures for impact-loaded components without running prohibitively expensive CPFE simulations at every design step.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D microstructures to spatiotemporal velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Stochastic microstructure generation plus derivative-free optimization explores candidate designs.
Distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) using MMD monitors out-of-distribution surrogate use.
evidence_signal: Optimized designs were validated with CPFE at under 3% prediction error, and surrogate-based optimization cut cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Performance depends on staying within a reliable microstructure distribution; extrapolation beyond the training set can undermine surrogate accuracy.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
